summary: Dependency-confusion lure exfiltrates host recon to webhook.site
details: math-helpers-extra-utils@1.0.1 is packaged to masquerade as an internal Wix Thunderbolt module: its manifest advertises a baseURL under static.parastorage.com (Wix's CDN) and exports module names such as thunderboltRegistry, editorRegistry, and corvidRegistry that mirror internal Wix SSR components. On load, thunderboltRegistry.js runs a top-level IIFE that executes the shell commands `id`, `hostname`, and `uname -a` via child_process.execSync and transmits their output together with the Node.js version, platform, architecture, and process id as query-string parameters to the hardcoded collector URL https://webhook.site/0492a36c-4d7b-408a-865c-226db25987ba. The package name does not correspond to a published Wix library, and the combination of Wix-internal naming, parastorage baseURL, and import-time exfiltration of build-host identifiers to a third-party webhook collector matches the dependency-confusion attack pattern against Wix build infrastructure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
